title: Geo-aware eviction + control-plane rollforward controller for Hosted API
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We observed that multi-region rollouts for Hosted API occasionally result in noisy regional degradations that are hard to isolate: a single region's upstream thermal throttling or network flaps can cause global routing oscillation or slow rollbacks. Current blue/green + weighted traffic shifting lacks a first-class notion of geo-eviction and fast control-plane rollforward to protect regional SLOs and reduce blast radius.

Goal: Implement a controller that coordinates geo-aware eviction (temporary regional traffic quarantine and controlled weight decay) with an accelerated control-plane rollforward path for safe fast promotion when upstream issues are transient. The controller should integrate SLO gates, error-budget checks, and an operator-overridable policy layer. It must be compatible with our existing routing table, canary weights, and LTS channel metadata.

Acceptance criteria:
- Controller can quarantine a region (set effective weight -> 0) based on configurable SLO violations (5xx spikes, p99 latency regressions) within 2 minutes of detection.
- Automated decay policy: gradual shift of traffic off a quarantined region with configurable half-life and emergency drain options.
- Fast rollforward path: when a region recovers (health checks green, p99 back under threshold), the control plane can resume promotion within configurable bounds and short-circuit remaining holdpoints under safe conditions.
- Integration tests exercising multi-region canary, simulated network partitions, and synthetic traffic with reproducible SLO metrics.
- Dashboard panels and alerting playbooks added to Console.
plan: Design policy schema (operator overrides, default SLO thresholds, decay curve parameters)
Prototype controller logic in staging cluster (k8s controller + control-plane service endpoint)
Wire in SLO signals: metrics exporter -> runbook rules -> controller webhook
Add safety gates: error budget checks, rollback triggers, maximum quarantine TTL
Create canary job matrix for multi-region traffic shaping and synthetic scenarios
Iterate on UX: Console panel for current quarantines, proposed rollforwards, and manual overrides
Ship initial alpha behind a feature flag and run against low-traffic customers
decision_log: 2025-02-15: Chose to implement controller in control plane rather than a service-side forwarder so routing decisions remain centralized and auditable.
2025-02-16: Trade-off: aggressive automatic quarantines reduce blast radius but increase customer-facing failovers; decided to require two independent SLO signals (error-rate and latency) by default.
2025-02-18: Opted for exponential decay curve with configurable half-life instead of fixed step weights to smooth traffic evacuation across heterogeneous regions.
2025-02-19: Decided to expose a one-click emergency rollback in Console that bypasses standard canary holdpoints when manual confirmation is provided by on-call with proper justification recorded.
Rationale: Centralized controller simplifies audits, enables consistent region-level policies, and works better with dedicated capacity deployments where we must respect isolation boundaries.
test_plan: Unit tests for policy parsing, signal aggregation, and quarantine state machine
Integration: run staged multi-region canary with synthetic 5xx injection in us-west-2 and verify quarantine within 120s
Chaos: simulate transient network partition and validate auto rollforward when healthchecks recover within configured window
Load test: ensure controller decisions scale to 2000 concurrent rollouts without overwhelming the control plane
SLO regression: baseline p50/p95/p99 before and after controller enabled to confirm no regression in normal steady-state
